previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a patient with relapsed multiple myeloma and recently diagnosed MDS with pancytopenia, was admitted for symptomatic hypercalcemia with a corrected calcium level of 13.8 and associated fatigue. He was treated with aggressive hydration, calcitonin, and pamidronate, leading to normalization of calcium levels by discharge. During the admission, he was found to have radiographic evidence of pneumonia, likely aspiration-related or infectious, and was treated with a 7-day course of levofloxacin. His mental status improved, and he remained stable throughout the stay. Revlimid was held during admission and resumed post-discharge. He was discharged home with instructions to complete antibiotics, monitor weight, and follow up with his oncologist and for a gallbladder ultrasound due to CT findings of sludge and pericholecystic fat stranding.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted to the hospital for hypercalcemia (high 
calcium level).  This was caused by your multiple myeloma and 
treated with IV fluids and pamidronate, a medication which draws 
calcium into the bones.  You should continue to receive this or 
similar medications (zoledronic acid = Zometa) as an outpatient 
on a regular basis, perhaps monthly.  You also had acute kidney 
injury, probably from dehydration and the high calcium.  This 
was also treated with IV fluids.  You should continue to drink 
plenty of non-caffeinated fluids, especially water.
.
Weigh yourself every morning, call MD if weight goes up more 
than 3 lbs.
.
MEDICATION CHANGES:
1. You should continue to medications to lower calcium, for 
example zoledronic acid (Zometa), as an outpatient on a regular 
basis, perhaps monthly.
2. Decrease acyclovir to 400mg 2x a day (dose based on kidney 
function).
3. You will need to discuss with your primary 
hematologist/oncologist about when to restart chemotherapy for 
multiple myeloma.
